item_name: Stage 2 Pressure Ulcers (M0300B1: Number of Stage 2 pressure ulcers; M0300B2: Number of these Stage 2 pressure ulcers that were present upon admission/entry or reentry)
lookback_notes: NOT_FOUND for M0300B itself. The M0300B coding instructions direct the assessor to count pressure ulcers that are "currently present" (p. M-13) and do not state a number of look-back days. A 7-day look-back is stated for the gateway item M0210 ("Code based on the presence of any pressure ulcer/injury (regardless of stage) in the past 7 days.", p. M-5), and the M0210 Planning-for-Care text refers to staging "during the look-back period" (p. M-4), but neither passage is stated as the M0300B observation window. Recorded as a conflict/ambiguity rather than inferred.

coding_levels.label: Number of Stage 2 pressure ulcers currently present
coding_levels.definition: Enter the number of pressure ulcers that are currently present and whose deepest anatomical stage is Stage 2.

source.quote: Enter the number of pressure ulcers that are currently present and whose deepest anatomical stage is Stage 2.

coding_levels.label: No Stage 2 pressure ulcers present
coding_levels.definition: Enter 0 if no Stage 2 pressure ulcers are present and skip to M0300C, Stage 3.

source.quote: Enter 0 if no Stage 2 pressure ulcers are present and skip to M0300C, Stage 3.

coding_levels.label: Number of these Stage 2 pressure ulcers present upon admission/entry or reentry
coding_levels.definition: Enter the number of these Stage 2 pressure ulcers that were first noted at the time of admission/entry AND—for residents who are reentering the facility after a hospital stay, enter the number of Stage 2 pressure ulcers that were acquired during the hospitalization.

source.quote: Enter the number of these Stage 2 pressure ulcers that were first noted at the time of admission/entry AND—for residents who are reentering the facility after a hospital stay, enter the number of Stage 2 pressure ulcers that were acquired during the hospitalization (i.e., the Stage 2 pressure ulcer was not acquired in the nursing facility prior to admission to the hospital).

coding_levels.label: No Stage 2 pressure ulcers first noted at admission/entry or reentry
coding_levels.definition: Enter 0 if no Stage 2 pressure ulcers were first noted at the time of admission/entry or reentry.

source.quote: Enter 0 if no Stage 2 pressure ulcers were first noted at the time of admission/entry or reentry.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Stage 2 is defined on the item as: partial thickness loss of dermis presenting as a shallow open ulcer with a red or pink wound bed, without slough; may also present as an intact or open/ruptured blister.

source.quote: Stage 2: Partial thickness loss of dermis presenting as a shallow open ulcer with a red or pink wound bed, without slough. May also present as an intact or open/ruptured blister

federal_coding_rules.rule: M0300B1: enter the number of pressure ulcers currently present whose deepest anatomical stage is Stage 2.

source.quote: Enter the number of pressure ulcers that are currently present and whose deepest anatomical stage is Stage 2.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If M0300B1 is 0, skip to M0300C, Stage 3.

source.quote: Number of Stage 2 pressure ulcers - If 0 → Skip to M0300C, Stage 3

federal_coding_rules.rule: M0300B2: enter the number of these Stage 2 pressure ulcers first noted at the time of admission/entry, and for residents reentering after a hospital stay, those acquired during the hospitalization (i.e., not acquired in the nursing facility prior to hospital admission); enter 0 if none.

source.quote: Enter the number of these Stage 2 pressure ulcers that were first noted at the time of admission/entry AND—for residents who are reentering the facility after a hospital stay, enter the number of Stage 2 pressure ulcers that were acquired during the hospitalization

federal_coding_rules.rule: Code here only if the lesion assessed is primarily related to pressure and other conditions have been ruled out; if pressure is not the primary cause, do not code here.

source.quote: For the purposes of coding, determine that the lesion being assessed is primarily related to pressure and that other conditions have been ruled out. If pressure is not the primary cause, do not code here.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Stage 2 pressure ulcers by definition have partial thickness loss of the dermis; granulation tissue, slough, and eschar are not present in Stage 2 pressure ulcers.

source.quote: Stage 2 pressure ulcers by definition have partial thickness loss of the dermis. Granulation tissue, slough, and eschar are not present in Stage 2 pressure ulcers.

federal_coding_rules.rule: Do not code skin tears, tape burns, moisture associated skin damage, or excoriation at M0300B.

source.quote: Do not code skin tears, tape burns, moisture associated skin damage, or excoriation here.

federal_coding_rules.rule: When a pressure ulcer presents as an intact blister, examine the adjacent and surrounding area for signs of deep tissue injury; when a deep tissue injury is determined, do not code as a Stage 2.

source.quote: When a pressure ulcer presents as an intact blister, examine the adjacent and surrounding area for signs of deep tissue injury. When a deep tissue injury is determined, do not code as a Stage 2.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If other conditions are ruled out and the tissue adjacent to or surrounding an intact blister demonstrates signs of tissue damage (e.g., color change, tenderness, bogginess or firmness, warmth or coolness), these characteristics suggest a deep tissue injury (DTI) rather than a Stage 2 pressure ulcer.

source.quote: If other conditions are ruled out and the tissue adjacent to or surrounding the blister demonstrates signs of tissue damage (e.g., color change, tenderness, bogginess or firmness, warmth or coolness), these characteristics suggest a deep tissue injury (DTI) rather than a Stage 2 pressure ulcer.

federal_coding_rules.rule: For each pressure ulcer, determine the deepest anatomical stage; at admission, code based on findings from the first skin assessment conducted on or after and as close to the admission as possible; do not reverse or back stage; consider current and historical levels of tissue involvement.

source.quote: For each pressure ulcer, determine the deepest anatomical stage. At admission, code based on findings from the first skin assessment that is conducted on or after and as close to the admission as possible. Do not reverse or back stage. Consider current and historical levels of tissue involvement.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If a stageable pressure ulcer has ever been classified at a higher numerical stage than what is observed now, it should continue to be classified at the higher numerical stage until healed unless it becomes unstageable.

source.quote: If the stageable pressure ulcer has ever been classified at a higher numerical stage than what is observed now, it should continue to be classified at the higher numerical stage until healed unless it becomes unstageable.

federal_coding_rules.rule: A previously closed pressure ulcer that opens again should be reported at its worst stage, unless currently presenting at a higher stage or unstageable.

source.quote: A previously closed pressure ulcer that opens again should be reported at its worst stage, unless currently presenting at a higher stage or unstageable.

federal_coding_rules.rule: "Present on admission" determination (referenced by M0300B step 5): for each pressure ulcer/injury, determine if it was present at the time of admission/entry or reentry and not acquired while the resident was in the care of the nursing home, considering current and historical levels of tissue involvement.

source.quote: For each pressure ulcer/injury, determine if the pressure ulcer/injury was present at the time of admission/entry or reentry and not acquired while the resident was in the care of the nursing home. Consider current and historical levels of tissue involvement.

federal_coding_rules.rule: If the pressure ulcer/injury was present on admission/entry or reentry and subsequently increased in numerical stage during the resident's stay, the pressure ulcer is coded at that higher stage, and that higher stage should not be considered as "present on admission."

source.quote: If the pressure ulcer/injury was present on admission/entry or reentry and subsequently increased in numerical stage during the resident's stay, the pressure ulcer is coded at that higher stage, and that higher stage should not be considered as "present on admission."

federal_coding_rules.rule: If a numerically stageable pressure ulcer/injury was present on admission/entry or reentry and becomes unstageable due to slough or eschar during the stay, it is coded at M0300F and should not be coded as "present on admission."

source.quote: If a numerically stageable pressure ulcer/injury was present on admission/entry or reentry and becomes unstageable due to slough or eschar, during the resident's stay, the pressure ulcer/injury is coded at M0300F and should not be coded as "present on admission."

federal_coding_rules.rule: If a resident with a facility-acquired pressure ulcer/injury is hospitalized and returns with that ulcer/injury at the same numerical stage, it should not be coded as "present on admission."

source.quote: If a resident who has a pressure ulcer/injury that was originally acquired in the facility is hospitalized and returns with that pressure ulcer/injury at the same numerical stage, the pressure ulcer/injury should not be coded as "present on admission"

federal_coding_rules.rule: If a resident with a pressure ulcer/injury that was "present on admission" is hospitalized and returns with that ulcer at the same numerical stage, it is still coded as "present on admission."

source.quote: If a resident who has a pressure ulcer/injury that was "present on admission" (not acquired in the facility) is hospitalized and returns with that pressure ulcer/injury at the same numerical stage, the pressure ulcer is still coded as "present on admission"

federal_coding_rules.rule: If a pressure ulcer/injury documented on admission closed and then reopens at the same stage (not a higher stage), the ulcer/injury is coded as "present on admission."

source.quote: If a resident has a pressure ulcer/injury that was documented on admission then closed that reopens at the same stage (i.e., not a higher stage), the ulcer/injury is coded as "present on admission."

federal_coding_rules.rule: If two pressure ulcers that were both "present on admission" merge, the merged ulcer continues to be coded as "present on admission"; there must be an increase in numerical stage or a change to unstageable due to slough or eschar for it to be considered not "present on admission."

source.quote: If two pressure ulcers merge, that were both "present on admission," continue to code the merged pressure ulcer as "present on admission."

federal.criterion: Perform a head-to-toe/full body skin assessment focusing on bony prominences and pressure-bearing areas (sacrum, buttocks, heels, ankles, etc.) as the basis for counting Stage 2 pressure ulcers.

source.quote: Perform head-to-toe assessment. Conduct a full body skin assessment focusing on bony prominences and pressure-bearing areas (sacrum, buttocks, heels, ankles, etc.).

federal.notes: Listed as Step 1 of Steps for Assessment for M0300B.

federal.criterion: Identify the number of these pressure ulcers that were present on admission/entry or reentry, following the instructions on page M-8.

source.quote: Identify the number of these pressure ulcers that were present on admission/entry or reentry (see instructions on page M-8).

federal.criterion: Review the history of each pressure ulcer in the medical record; nursing homes that carefully document and track pressure ulcers will be able to more accurately code this item.

source.quote: Review the history of each pressure ulcer in the medical record.

federal.notes: From Step 1 (Determine Deepest Anatomical Stage) for M0300A–G.

federal.criterion: Review the medical record for the history of the ulcer/injury when determining "present on admission."

source.quote: Review the medical record for the history of the ulcer/injury.

federal.notes: Step 3, item 1, referenced by M0300B step 5.

federal.criterion: Review for location and stage at the time of admission/entry or reentry.

source.quote: Review for location and stage at the time of admission/entry or reentry.

federal.notes: Step 3, item 2, referenced by M0300B step 5.

federal.criterion: Nursing homes may document the healing of pressure ulcers using descriptive characteristics of the wound (depth, width, presence or absence of granulation tissue, etc.) or by using a validated pressure ulcer healing tool (reverse/back-staging is not used).

source.quote: Nursing homes can document the healing of pressure ulcers using descriptive characteristics of the wound (i.e., depth, width, presence or absence of granulation tissue, etc.) or by using a validated pressure ulcer healing tool.

federal.notes: Framed as an option ("can document"), not a required record element.

case_mix_relevance.notes: The supplied Section M pages do not tie M0300B to a payment or case-mix classification. A scenario on p. M-43 references a PPS 5-day assessment, but no payment/case-mix grouping is stated for this item.

positions.claim: M0300B coding instructions count pressure ulcers that are "currently present," with no stated number of look-back days.

source.quote: Enter the number of pressure ulcers that are currently present and whose deepest anatomical stage is Stage 2.

positions.claim: The gateway item M0210, which routes the assessor to M0300, is coded on presence of any pressure ulcer/injury in the past 7 days (7-day look-back period).

source.quote: Code based on the presence of any pressure ulcer/injury (regardless of stage) in the past 7 days.

positions.claim: Section M Planning-for-Care text states that initial numerical staging should be coded in terms of what is assessed during the look-back period.

source.quote: initial numerical staging of pressure ulcers and the initial numerical staging of ulcers after debridement, or DTI that declares itself, should be coded in terms of what is assessed (seen or palpated, i.e. visible tissue, palpable bone) during the look-back period
